questions.stem: The bearing of B from A is 065 degrees. What is the bearing of A from B?
questions.explanation: To find the back bearing, add 180 degrees: 065 + 180 = 245 degrees. Since 245 is less than 360, the bearing of A from B is 245 degrees.

questions.stem: A ship sails on a bearing of 135 degrees. In which general direction is it heading?
questions.explanation: Bearings are measured clockwise from north. 135 degrees is between 90 degrees (East) and 180 degrees (South), so the direction is South-East.

questions.stem: The bearing of C from B is 210 degrees. What is the bearing of B from C?
questions.explanation: Back bearing = 210 + 180 = 390 degrees. Since this exceeds 360, subtract 360: 390 - 360 = 030 degrees.

questions.stem: Town A is due north of town C. Town B is on a bearing of 065 degrees from A. If angle ACB = 40 degrees, what is angle ABC?
questions.explanation: The bearing from A to B is 065 degrees, so angle BAC = 65 degrees. In triangle ABC: angle ABC = 180 - 65 - 40 = 75 degrees.

questions.stem: A hiker walks 5 km on a bearing of 090 degrees (due east) then 5 km on a bearing of 000 degrees (due north). What is the straight-line distance from the starting point?
questions.explanation: The two legs are perpendicular (east then north). By Pythagoras: distance = sqrt(5^2 + 5^2) = sqrt(50) = 5 sqrt(2) km, which is approximately 7.07 km.
